subject: community-medicine
title: Iodine Deficiency Disorders: Goitre Grading, Salt Iodisation and NIDDCP

steps.title: A spectrum, not just a swelling
steps.tx: **Iodine deficiency disorders** span the life course: abortion and stillbirth, neonatal hypothyroidism, cretinism with deaf-mutism and intellectual disability, goitre at all ages, and impaired cognition in schoolchildren losing measurable IQ points. Framing deficiency as only a neck swelling is the historical error the spectrum concept was coined to kill.
steps.say: Deficiency writes across a lifetime. Lost pregnancies, cretinism, deaf-mutism, dull schooling, goitre last. The spectrum framing exists because neck swellings were the least of the damage all along.

steps.title: Goitre grading at survey speed
steps.tx: **Goitre grading** runs Grade 0 (no palpable or visible goitre), Grade 1 (palpable but not visible with neck in normal position), Grade 2 (visible with neck normal). Total goitre rate above 5 percent in school-age children marks a public health problem. Palpation surveys of 6 to 12 year olds are the standard field instrument.
steps.say: Three grades, fingers and eyes. Palpable only, then visible at rest. Over five percent in schoolchildren declares a public health problem. School surveys by palpation remain the standard field instrument.

rows: Palpable, not visible in normal position

steps.tx: **Goitre grading** uses fingers and eyes with the neck in a normal position. Grade 0 means no palpable or visible goitre. Grade 1 is palpable but not visible at rest. Grade 2 is visible while the neck stays in that normal position, as in a schoolchild examined face on. A total goitre rate above five percent in school age children marks a public health problem. Palpation surveys of children aged six to twelve years are the standard field instrument.
steps.say: Grade 0 goitre is neither felt nor seen. Grade 1 is felt but hidden when the neck is in a normal position. Grade 2 is visible at rest. Above five percent in schoolchildren, iodine deficiency is a public health problem. Palpation of six to twelve year olds is the field method.

vis.alt: A schoolchild neck, held in a normal position, shows a goitre that is visible without being asked to swallow.
vis.caption: With the neck at rest, a schoolchild thyroid swelling is already visible, fitting grade 2 goitre. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Urinary iodine reads the present
steps.tx: **Median urinary iodine** in schoolchildren judges current intake at population level: under 20 micrograms per litre severe deficiency, 20 to 49 moderate, 50 to 99 mild, 100 to 199 adequate. Individuals vary day to day, so medians of groups, never single urines, classify districts. Neonatal TSH screening adds a sensitive newborn window.
steps.say: Urine reads the present, groups only. Median under twenty severe, one hundred to one ninety nine adequate in schoolchildren. Single urines mislead by daily variation; district medians classify. Newborn TSH adds a sensitive second window.

steps.title: Salt iodisation: the vehicle logic
steps.tx: **Universal salt iodisation** chose salt because everyone eats it daily in small steady amounts, production is centralised enough to fortify, and cost stays paise per person yearly. Potassium iodate suits tropical stability better than iodide. India mandates iodised salt nationally, banning non-iodised salt for human consumption in programme design, with 30 ppm at production and 15 ppm at consumer level as the classic standards.
steps.say: Salt carries iodine because everyone eats a little daily and factories are few. Iodate survives tropics better. Thirty parts per million at production, fifteen at the consumer's kitchen in classic standards.

steps.tx: **Universal salt iodisation** uses salt because people eat a little of it every day, production is centralised enough to fortify, and the cost stays a few paise per person each year. Potassium iodate holds up in tropical heat better than iodide. India mandates iodised salt for human consumption and, in programme design, bans non iodised salt. Classic standards are thirty parts per million at production and fifteen parts per million at the consumer kitchen, which is what a spot kit checks.
steps.say: Salt was chosen for iodine because intake is daily, small, and factory based, at tiny cost. Iodate survives heat better than iodide. Classic levels are thirty parts per million at the plant and fifteen in the kitchen, the figure a spot kit is built to check.

vis.alt: An iodised salt packet marked fifteen parts per million at consumer level sits beside a spot testing kit.
vis.caption: A salt packet labelled fifteen parts per million iodine sits next to a field spot testing kit. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Daily requirement and the pregnancy premium
steps.tx: **Daily iodine need** is about 150 micrograms for adults, rising to roughly 250 in pregnancy and lactation, against goitrogenic pressures from cassava and cruciferous thiocyanates in some ecologies. The fetal brain taxes the premium: deficiency in the first half of pregnancy damages neurodevelopment irreversibly before goitre appears in anyone.
steps.say: Pregnancy pays the premium: one fifty rising toward two fifty micrograms daily. Fetal brains suffer first and permanently, before any neck swells. Goitrogen foods add pressure in cassava ecologies.

steps.title: NIDDCP machinery
steps.tx: The **National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme** (from the 1962 goitre control programme, renamed 1992) runs surveys, supplies iodised salt, checks salt iodine at production and retail (spot kits qualitatively, titration quantitatively), and educates against stored-salt iodine loss. District resurveys every few years verify that elimination sustains, because goitre memory outlives intake correction by years.
steps.say: Programme machinery surveys, supplies, tests and teaches. Salt checked at factory and shop, districts resurveyed on rotation. Goitre shrinks years behind intake correction, so vigilance outlasts early victories.

steps.title: Storage and cooking losses at home
steps.tx: **Household losses** silently defeat factory dosing: salt stored open near heat, bought loose from humid sacks, or added early to prolonged boiling loses iodine before eating. Teaching points are concrete: closed dry storage away from the stove, purchase of packaged iodised salt, and late addition in cooking where habits allow. Salt test kits in community hands make the invisible visible during campaigns.
steps.say: Kitchens undo factories. Open storage by the stove, humid loose sacks, long boiling: iodine leaves before eating. Closed dry jars, packaged salt and late addition are the teachable fixes.

right.title: Iodine kept
points: Closed dry container away from stove

steps.title: Excess and the U-shaped caution
steps.tx: **Iodine excess** after rapid correction can trigger iodine-induced hyperthyroidism in older nodular goitre patients and autoimmune flares at population extremes, so monitoring includes harm surveillance during scale-up. The dose-response is U-shaped: deficiency and excess both injure thyroid function. This caution refines, never reverses, iodisation policy in deficient populations.
steps.say: Correction carries a small backlash. Older nodular glands can tip into hyperthyroidism as iodine returns, so scale-up watches for harm. The curve is U-shaped; that refines dosing vigilance, never reverses policy.

steps.title: Elimination criteria districts aim at
steps.tx: **Elimination as a public health problem** is certified by combined indicators: total goitre rate under 5 percent in schoolchildren, median urinary iodine at or above 100, over 90 percent households consuming adequately iodised salt (15 ppm or more), and neonatal TSH signals low. No single indicator certifies alone, the composite logic examiners test with district data sets.
steps.say: Certification is composite. Goitre under five percent, urinary medians adequate, nine of ten households on properly iodised salt, newborn signals quiet. Single indicators never certify alone in examination data sets.
